helpers.name: aimfp_run

parameters.name: is_new_session
parameters.description: Whether this is a new session start. Use true for first interaction, new session, or after long breaks. Use false (default) for continuation work.

helpers.purpose: Main entry point orchestrator. Called on session start (is_new_session=true) for full context bundle, and at work checkpoints (is_new_session=false) for watchdog alerts only.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error message if database not accessible. Returns empty suggestions if no directives match.
return_statements: [when:initialized=false] No AIMFP project in this directory. Offer aimfp_init(project_root), or restore_project_backup if the user has a backup.

[when:user_settings.project_continue_on_start=true] AUTOSTART (project_continue_on_start=true): continue the work in data.status.position without waiting for a command. Resume the focused work, or present the open tasks by priority and start the first.
[when:migration.pending] Schema migrations are pending (data.migration.pending): tell the user, then call migrate_databases() and follow its return statements.

[when:migration.unreadable] data.migration.unreadable lists databases that could NOT BE READ (locked, damaged, or held by another process): their migration status is unknown. Report each to the user. Never run migrate_databases to 'fix' them: that rebuild is for old schemas, not unreadable files.

[when:deferred_notes] data.deferred_notes lists deferred work (metadata only). Read the ones relevant to the current work with get_notes_comprehensive(note_id=X); resolved ones → update_note(note_type='completed').

[when:watchdog.reminders] WATCHDOG: handle each reminder in data.watchdog.reminders (deleted, unregistered or changed files), then call clear_watchdog(). A structure_gaps reminder is recomputed from project.db at every checkpoint and stays until the gaps are fixed.
[when:backup] data.backup: an inactivity backup was just created. Mention it to the user.

[when:project_root_rewritten] PROJECT MOVED OR COPIED: data.project_root_rewritten means the recorded project location was out of date and has been updated to data.project_root. For reason 'moved_or_copied', tell the user once (original_exists=true means this folder is a copy and the original project's database is untouched); reason 'worktree' is expected in a git worktree and needs no mention. Do NOT call update_project_root: it is already fixed. data.source_directory_rewritten (an absolute source path made relative) needs no action.
implementation_notes: is_new_session=true: {project_root, status (aimfp_status 'summary' tier, includes the core supportive_context), user_settings {key: value}, supportive_context_coding (only once a milestone exists), supportive_context_case2 (Case 2 only), watchdog, case_2_context, backup (only when one was taken), scheduled_backup (only when due), notices (only when pending), migration {pending, unreadable} (only when something needs action), deferred_notes}. Keys with nothing to report are omitted.
is_new_session=false: {watchdog: {status, reminders[], notice}} when reminders exist, {} otherwise.

Return statements follow the payload: aimfp_run's own statements are gated on the keys they talk about ([when:path] tags, helpers/shared/return_gates.py), and each bundled section present brings its owning tool's statements (status → aimfp_status, notices → get_pending_notices, scheduled_backup → check_scheduled_backup_due, case_2_context.health → check_directive_health). A checkpoint with nothing to report returns no statements (custom user statements excepted).

Watchdog status values: 'ok' (running, checked), 'starting' (just launched, PID not yet registered — do not restart), 'failed' (launch failed — surface start_error), 'not_running' (PID file missing — inform user), 'no_reminders_file' (PID exists but reminders missing — watchdog may have failed), 'external' (embedding host passed start_watchdog=False and runs its own watcher), 'disabled' (server started with --no-watchdog; the host runs its own watcher — reminders still reported, no action), 'no_project' (no project found). AI should surface notice to user when status is 'failed', 'not_running' or 'no_reminders_file'.
Structure gaps reach the watchdog as ONE structure_gaps reminder (counts by kind); aimfp_status lists the gaps on the active work, get_structure_health lists all.
Directive names and the FP directive index are NOT bundled: get_all_directive_names / get_fp_directive_index / search_directives on demand.
Does NOT parse user input or match intent - returns data only

used_by_directives.description: aimfp_run directive uses aimfp_run helper as entry point orchestrator

helpers.name: aimfp_init
helpers.purpose: Phase 1 mechanical setup orchestrator for project initialization. Atomically creates directories, databases with schemas, and templates. No deep logic - pure mechanical operations.
helpers.error_handling: Return detailed error if: already initialized, directory permissions denied, database creation failed. Clean up partial initialization on error, removing only what this init created: the whole .aimfp-project/ if init created it, otherwise just the created databases/blueprint/backups dir (pre-existing files such as backups survive).
return_statements: Verify initialization: confirm .aimfp-project/ exists with project.db, user_preferences.db, ProjectBlueprint.md and backups/. Report any issues to user before proceeding.

Phase 1 complete. AI must now execute Phase 2: scan for OOP patterns (if existing code), detect infrastructure (language, build tool, source directory), and prompt user for project name/purpose/goals. IMPORTANT: The project table is EMPTY after Phase 1. AI must call create_project(name, purpose, goals, status, version) as the FIRST step of Phase 2 to insert the project row. Do NOT call update_project before create_project — there is no row to update yet.

Phase 2 ordering: (1) create_project — must complete first, (2) update_source_directory + update infrastructure entries — can run in parallel after create_project succeeds, (3) populate ProjectBlueprint.md. Do NOT batch create_project with infrastructure updates in one parallel call.

Empty infrastructure entries created: project_root (populated), source_directory, primary_language, build_tool, package_manager, test_framework, runtime_version, main_branch. AI must detect and populate these using update_project_entry(table='infrastructure', id=N, data={'value': '...'}) — only the 'value' field should be updated (not 'description' or 'details'). Call get_all_infrastructure() first to see current IDs and values.
ProjectBlueprint.md is a template with placeholders. AI must populate it with real project data after user interaction.
[when:git_status=created] .git was initialized by this init: run the git_init directive during project_discovery (gitignore, initial commit, hash storage, branch detection).
[when:git_status=pre_existing] A git repository already existed: run the git_init directive during project_discovery (gitignore review, hash storage, branch detection).
[when:git_status=git_unavailable] git is not available (command missing or failed): tell the user version control is unavailable and suggest installing git.

After Phase 2 population complete: route to project_discovery directive. Discovery handles: git_init directive (intelligent Git setup if git available), collaborative blueprint refinement, infrastructure confirmation, state database creation (via create_state_database helper once source_directory is confirmed), the MODULARITY LAYER — themes (stable project areas), flows (behaviour, each linked to >= 1 theme via add_flow theme_ids), modules (reusable code boundaries mapped to directory seams) — then completion paths linked to their themes and milestones linked to their flows. Do not skip the modularity layer: every file you reserve later must declare its flows.

Do NOT create state database during init — source_directory is not yet confirmed. State DB creation happens during project_discovery Branch 3 (map_infrastructure) after source_directory is confirmed with user.

[when:files_already_present] data.files_already_present: init never overwrites existing files, so these (commonly .watchdogignore or ProjectBlueprint.md) were left as found and may be stale or belong to another project. Read each one and reconcile it with this project — confirm a pre-existing ProjectBlueprint.md with the user before relying on or replacing it. Only data.files_created were freshly written from templates.
implementation_notes: PHASE 1 ONLY - Mechanical setup with no intelligence
Step 1: Check if already initialized (error if .aimfp-project/project.db exists). Then snapshot which init artifacts already exist on disk — drives both the report and failure cleanup
Step 2: Create directories: .aimfp-project/, .aimfp-project/backups/

Step 2.5: Check for .git directory. If missing and git available, run 'git init' (subprocess, non-blocking, 10s timeout). Store result as git_status: 'created' (new repo), 'pre_existing' (already had .git), or 'git_unavailable' (git not found or failed). Initialization continues regardless of git outcome.
Step 3: Copy ProjectBlueprint_template.md to .aimfp-project/ProjectBlueprint.md only if absent (a surviving blueprint is never overwritten); the init evolution note says which case occurred

Step 4: Initialize project.db: load schemas/project.sql, execute, then execute initialization/standard_infrastructure.sql (8 empty entries), then call update_project_root() to populate project_root value
Step 5: Initialize user_preferences.db: load schemas/user_preferences.sql, execute, INSERT default tracking_settings (all disabled), load initialization/standard_user_settings.sql (backup defaults)
Step 6: Create .gitkeep files for empty directories
Step 6.5: Write .watchdogignore to project root from DEFAULT_WATCHDOGIGNORE_CONTENT (watchdog/config.py). Idempotent — skip if it already exists.
Step 7: Verify all created files exist (inline check, no helper call)
Step 8: Return success object

RETURN STRUCTURE: {success: bool, project_root: str, aimfp_dir: str, files_created: [labels written by this init], files_already_present: [labels found in place and left untouched], tables_created: {project_db: [...], user_prefs_db: [...]}, infrastructure_entries: 8, git_status: 'created'|'pre_existing'|'skipped'|'git_unavailable', next_phase: 'AI populates infrastructure and blueprint'}. Labels: '.aimfp-project/', '.aimfp-project/backups/', '.aimfp-project/project.db', '.aimfp-project/user_preferences.db', '.aimfp-project/ProjectBlueprint.md', '.watchdogignore'
State database is NOT created during init. It is created during project_discovery (Branch 3: map_infrastructure) via create_state_database() helper after source_directory is confirmed with user.
State DB reference: SQL schema at src/aimfp/database/initialization/state_db.sql, template at src/aimfp/templates/state_db/state_operations.py, helper at helpers/project/state_db.py

ERROR CLEANUP: If any step fails after Step 1, remove only what this init created (pure cleanup_targets_for_failed_init): all of .aimfp-project/ if init created the directory, otherwise just the created backups dir/.gitkeep/project.db/user_preferences.db/ProjectBlueprint.md. Partial initialization is worse than no initialization, but pre-existing files (e.g. backups beside a lost project.db) must survive.
ERROR RETURN: {success: false, error: str, failed_step: int, cleanup_performed: bool}
All operations are direct file/DB operations - no external helper calls

parameters_mapping.project_root: from current working directory or user input

used_by_directives.description: aimfp_init directive calls aimfp_init for Phase 1 mechanical setup

helpers.name: aimfp_status

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Tier: 'quick' (default) = position only (path, milestone, focused work with item names, their flows/themes, other open work, structure gap count), for completion loops and 'where am I' checks. 'summary' = full reload after lost or compacted context (adds core supportive context, purpose/goals, infrastructure, recent files with flows/themes/module, recent notes, history). 'detailed' = summary + full work tree.

helpers.purpose: Project status in three tiers. Default 'quick' is the cheap position check for completion loops; 'summary' is the reload after lost or compacted context. Structure (themes/flows/modules) is attached to the work and files shown, never listed whole.
helpers.error_handling: Returns {initialized: false} if .aimfp-project/ does not exist.
return_statements: [when:initialized=false] Not initialized: route to aimfp_init.
[when:tier=quick] Lost or compacted context? Call aimfp_status(type='summary') for the full reload (core supportive context, purpose/goals, recent files, notes).
[when:discovery_pending] No completion path or milestone yet: discovery comes first. Load get_directive_by_name('project_discovery') before creating any task.
[when:position] Priority for current focus: sidequests → subtasks → tasks.
[when:position.reserved] position.reserved lists files/functions reserved but never finalized: finalize them (finalize_file / finalize_functions) or remove them (delete_reserved).

[when:structure.active_gaps] structure.active_gaps lists modularity gaps on the work in front of you. Fix them before continuing: add_flow_themes, add_path_themes, add_milestone_flows, add_file_flows, add_files_to_module, update_file(no_flow_reason=...). New behaviour with no fitting flow → add_flow(name, theme_ids) + add_milestone_flows; never stretch an unrelated flow.
[when:structure.total_gaps] structure.total_gaps counts every modularity gap in the project; get_structure_health() lists them. Tell the user the count and fix them in batches this session.

[when:stored_root_mismatch] stored_root_mismatch: the recorded project location ({stored}) is not this folder ({live}): the project was moved or copied, or this is a git worktree. Reads and writes already use this folder's database; aimfp_run(is_new_session=true) updates the record. Do not call update_project_root with the stored path.
implementation_notes: Tiers are shaped by pure functions in helpers/orchestrators/status_payload.py; aimfp_status only gathers rows

position: path, milestone (with flows+themes), focus (task/subtask/sidequest with flows+themes and item names/status), open_tasks/sidequests of that milestone (names only), blocked and reserved when present
The milestone is the focused work's own milestone when there is focus (subtask -> parent task, sidequest -> paused task)
structure: total_gaps for the whole project + active_gaps touching the active path/milestone/flows/recent files (focus_structure_gaps); omitted when there are no gaps

summary adds: project purpose/goals, infrastructure as {values, unset}, recent_files annotated with flows/themes/module, history, recent_notes (7 days, metadata only), active branches, core supportive_context
discovery_pending is set when no milestone exists yet
Keys with nothing to report are omitted (drop_empty); statements are gated on the payload (helpers/shared/return_gates.py)
aimfp_run(is_new_session=true) embeds the 'summary' tier; build_status_bundle embeds 'summary' minus supportive_context

used_by_directives.description: aimfp_status directive uses aimfp_status helper to retrieve comprehensive project state - AI determines next steps from returned data
Called by aimfp_run when is_new_session=true - provides comprehensive status for fresh context
Read current path/milestone/task state before deciding which progression branch applies

helpers.name: get_project_status
helpers.purpose: Retrieve work hierarchy data from project database. Returns structured counts, records, and nested tree in a single pass.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if project.db not found or not accessible.
return_statements: Files and functions may be reserved (is_reserved=1) but not finalized. Complete the reserve → write with ID in name → finalize flow before continuing.

Check reserved_entities for any functions/types with null fields (purpose, parameters, returns for functions; description for types). Populate missing fields via update_function/update_type before continuing.
implementation_notes: Summary returns: {counts{completion_paths, milestones, tasks, subtasks, sidequests, incomplete_*, blocked_items, modules}, hierarchy{active_path, active_milestone, active_tasks[], active_subtasks[], active_sidequests[], current_focus, active_items[], historical{}, recent_files[], reserved_entities{}}, blocked_items[]}
Hierarchy follows: completion_path → milestone → task/subtask/sidequest → items
Historical context is positional: last completed task in active milestone + items, last completed milestone if first task or no tasks
Reserved entities: files/functions with is_reserved=1 (not yet finalized)
Recent files: last 5 by updated_at
Detailed returns: full history with all records + nested tree
Type='quick': Counts and current in_progress item only
Type='summary': Hierarchy-aware context with positional history (default)
Type='detailed': All records including completed history + complete tree
NO analysis logic - returns raw data, AI interprets meaning

used_by_directives.description: Sub-helper used by aimfp_status to retrieve work hierarchy data (completion paths, milestones, tasks, subtasks, sidequests) with counts and nested tree

helpers.name: get_task_context

parameters.name: task_type
parameters.description: Type of task: 'task', 'subtask', 'sidequest'. Auto-detected from task_id if omitted.

parameters.name: detail_level
parameters.description: 'lean' (default): the work item in full; items with descriptions only while open; flows id/name; files with their functions as id/name; modules id/name/path/purpose. 'full': every record as stored (function purpose/parameters/returns, flow and item descriptions).

helpers.purpose: Get complete context for resuming work on a specific task/subtask/sidequest. Single call retrieves item + associated items + linked files + their functions and modules + flows + optionally interactions and notes. Files are linked automatically when reserved, finalized, cataloged, or updated (and when their functions/types are finalized, cataloged, or updated) while a work item is in_progress — the most recent in_progress sidequest, else subtask, else task. A task's context includes its subtasks' files. Uses cached project root internally.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if task not found or project.db not accessible.
return_statements: Task context loaded. AI should review items to determine where to resume.
If task is blocked: check blocked_by field and resolve blockers first.

BEFORE RESUMING WORK: Review the flows[] in the returned context (and the task's flow_ids — a file you add must declare one of them, or a new flow if none fits) — they describe the intended architecture and user-facing behavior. Use the returned files[] and functions as your lookup index BEFORE reading source files.
MODULES: Review modules[] to see which code boundaries the task touches. If multiple modules appear, consider cross-module impacts via get_module_dependencies().
If files[] is empty but work was done on this item (e.g. before it was in_progress): link the files with link_files_to_task(task_id, file_ids, task_type), then re-check.

[when:detail_level=lean] Lean context: function signatures, flow descriptions and completed items' descriptions are left out. Get them for what you are touching with get_functions_by_file(file_id) / get_function_by_name / get_flow_by_name, or call again with detail_level='full'.

[when:notes] notes lists the notes attached to the returned task/subtask/sidequest (without include_history; with it, notes holds the full note history) as references (id, type, severity, reference_id). Read the ones relevant to your work in full with get_notes_comprehensive(note_id=X) before acting; a deferred note you resolve -> update_note(note_type='completed').
implementation_notes: Returns: {task_item{}, task_type, items[], flows[], files[], functions[], modules[] (distinct modules owning task files), interactions[]?, notes[]?}
If task_type omitted: searches tasks, subtasks, sidequests tables by task_id and auto-detects type
Uses get_cached_project_root() — no project_root parameter needed
Gets associated items from items table (polymorphic: reference_table + reference_id)
Gets files from task_files (polymorphic: reference_table + reference_id); for task_type='task' also its subtasks' files
Gets flows: the item's own flow_ids, then flows of the linked files via file_flows
Gets functions for those files
If include_interactions=true: gets interactions for those functions
If include_history=true: gets notes for this task
Optimized for session resumption - everything needed to continue work in one call

used_by_directives.description: Load complete task context for resuming interrupted work - retrieves task details, associated flows, files, functions, interactions, and note history in single optimized query
Completion gate: confirm files[] lists every file worked on for the task before marking it complete

helpers.name: get_open_work

parameters.name: milestone_id
parameters.description: Limit to tasks of one milestone (and their subtasks and sidequests). Omit for all open work.

parameters.name: include_descriptions
parameters.description: Add truncated descriptions to each task, subtask and sidequest. Off keeps the payload small.

helpers.purpose: Every open task (pending, in_progress, blocked) with its open items and open subtasks (each with open items), plus open sidequests with their open items, in one read-only call. Ordered in_progress first, then by priority. Replaces get_incomplete_tasks followed by one get_items_for_task per task.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if the project root is not established or project.db is not accessible.
return_statements: Open work loaded. Continue the first in_progress task (tasks are ordered in_progress, pending, blocked, then by priority); a sidequest listed with a paused_task_id interrupts that task and comes first.
Need files, flows or functions for one of these? get_task_context(task_id) returns them for a single task.
implementation_notes: Returns: {tasks[{id, name, status, priority, milestone_id, description?, items[{id, name, status}], subtasks[{id, name, status, priority, description?, items[]}]}], sidequests[{id, name, status, priority, paused_task_id, description?, items[]}], counts{tasks, subtasks, sidequests, open_items}}
Open = status != 'completed'. Items are filtered the same way.
Pure assembly in assemble_open_work; four SELECTs, no writes.

helpers.name: get_current_progress

parameters.name: detail_level
parameters.description: 'minimal' (counts), 'lean' (default: key columns, open work first, 50 rows), 'full' (every column, every row). 'standard' is accepted as 'lean'.

helpers.purpose: Single entry point for scoped project status queries. Replaces 5-10 separate helper calls with one flexible query.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if project.db not found. Returns empty results for unknown scope.
return_statements: Rows are lean by default (key columns, open work first, at most 50; count is exact). detail_level='full' returns every column and row; get_task_context(task_id) gives one task's detail.
implementation_notes: Returns: Flexible object based on scope and detail_level parameters
Routes to appropriate table queries based on scope value
Applies filters as WHERE conditions
Default detail_level='standard' returns reasonable data without overwhelming
scope=null returns summary counts for all entity types

helpers.name: update_project_state

parameters.name: create_note
parameters.description: Auto-log action as note in notes table

helpers.purpose: Orchestrated state change for tasks, milestones, and paths. Maps actions (start_task, complete_task, block_task, etc.) to correct status updates and note creation.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if entity not found or invalid action for entity type.
return_statements: State updated. If task completed: check if all tasks in milestone are complete, consider marking milestone complete.
If task blocked: create sidequest to resolve blocker, then unblock and resume.

If task started (action=start_task): BEFORE CODING — check get_all_flows() and get_task_flows(task_id) for relevant workflow descriptions. Use DB lookups (get_function_by_name, get_type_by_name, get_functions_by_file) to understand existing code BEFORE reading source files.
implementation_notes: Returns: {success, updated_entity{}, note_created?, note_id?}
Maps action to appropriate field updates (status, timestamps)

Actions: start_task, complete_task, pause_task, resume_task, block_task, unblock_task, start_subtask, complete_subtask, start_sidequest, complete_sidequest, start_milestone, complete_milestone, start_path, complete_path
Updates entity status field and related timestamps
If create_note=true: inserts note record automatically with action context
Simplifies common state transitions with action-based interface

helpers.name: batch_update_progress

parameters.name: updates
parameters.description: List of update objects: [{target_type, target_id, action, data}, ...]

parameters.name: continue_on_error
parameters.description: Stop on first error or continue processing remaining updates

helpers.purpose: Update multiple project items atomically. Used after code generation or bulk operations to ensure consistency.
helpers.error_handling: Returns per-update results. If transaction=true and any fail, rolls back all.
return_statements: Batch update complete. Review any failures and retry individually if needed.
implementation_notes: Returns: {success, updated_count, failed_count, results[{success, entity, error?}]}
Iterates updates, calls update_project_state for each
Transaction=true: wraps in DB transaction for atomicity
Continue_on_error=true: processes all updates even if some fail
If transaction=true and any fail: rolls back all changes

helpers.name: query_project_state

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: WHERE-like conditions with operators: {field: value} or {field: {op: 'gt', value: 5}}

parameters.name: joins
parameters.description: Relations to include via LEFT JOIN: ['milestones', 'files']

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: ORDER BY clause: 'field ASC' or 'field DESC'

helpers.purpose: Flexible SQL-like query interface for complex project queries. Provides powerful filtering and joining capabilities without writing raw SQL.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error for unknown entity names or invalid filter operators.
implementation_notes: Returns: Array of entity objects with joins embedded
Filter operators: eq, ne, gt, lt, gte, lte, in, like
Joins uses predefined LEFT JOIN mappings (e.g., entity='tasks' + joins=['milestones'] -> LEFT JOIN milestones ON tasks.milestone_id = milestones.id)
Sort: 'field ASC' or 'field DESC'
Powerful SQL-like interface without writing raw SQL
Prevents SQL injection by parameterizing all values

helpers.name: get_files_by_flow_context

parameters.name: flow_id
parameters.description: Flow ID to get files for

helpers.purpose: Get all files for a flow with functions embedded in each file dict.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if flow not found or project.db not accessible.
implementation_notes: Returns: Array of file objects with functions[] embedded in each
Step 1: Query file_flows for flow_id -> get file_ids
Step 2: Query files for those file_ids
Step 3: For each file: query functions WHERE file_id = file.id
Step 4: Embed functions array in each file dict
Provides complete view of flow implementation

used_by_directives.description: Get all files implementing a flow with embedded functions - used to build dependency map showing file-flow-function relationships

helpers.name: migrate_databases
helpers.purpose: Migrate all pending project databases to current schema versions. Creates fresh DBs from new schema SQL, transfers data via ATTACH, returns temp paths for AI to verify and place.
helpers.error_handling: Returns per-DB results with verification data. Never throws — errors are captured per-DB.
return_statements: REFUSALS: report every data.skipped[] entry whose reason says migration was REFUSED. A refusal means the database contradicted itself — it reported version 0.0 while carrying tables, or while carrying a schema_version table whose row is unreadable — which indicates damage or a concurrent writer, NOT an old schema. NEVER present a refused database as 'up to date' or 'nothing to migrate'. Tell the user which database was refused and why, and leave it alone: it is untouched on disk and safe to inspect.
Verify all tables in each migrated DB show match=true in verification data
Move each backup from temp path to {project_root}/{aimfp_folder}/backups/{db_name}_pre_migration_v{old_version}_{YYYYMMDD}.db
Replace each old DB with new: move new_db_temp_path to original_db_path
Ask user about backup retention (delete old backups, keep, or cycle)
implementation_notes: Reads expected_schema_versions from aimfp_core.db to determine which DBs need migration
For each pending DB: backup old → create new from schema → ATTACH old → transfer shared columns → verify row counts
Schema-only: no init SQL (standard_infrastructure.sql etc.) — data comes from old DB
Triggers are AFTER UPDATE only, so INSERT transfers preserve original timestamps
Uses INSERT OR IGNORE to handle any constraint changes gracefully
Returns temp paths — tool does NOT move files, AI handles placement via return_statements

RETURN STRUCTURE: {migrated: [{db_name, old_version, new_version, backup_temp_path, new_db_temp_path, original_db_path, verification: {table: {old_rows, new_rows, match}}, warnings}], skipped: [], already_current: []}

helpers.name: aimfp_end
helpers.purpose: Session termination orchestrator. Gathers session audit data: reads watchdog state and final reminders, queries all files and functions from DB for AI to cross-reference, reads recent notes and task state. Stops watchdog process if running. Returns structured audit data for AI to interpret and act on. No analysis logic — AI determines what is stale or missing.
helpers.error_handling: Returns {initialized: false} if .aimfp-project/ does not exist. Returns partial data if watchdog PID file missing (watchdog not implemented or not running). Never fails hard — always returns what it can gather.
return_statements: AI should compare returned file/function lists against session work to identify untracked items.
AI should review returned task/milestone state for any needed progress updates.

MODULARITY REVIEW: data.structure_health lists gaps in themes/flows/modules. Fix the ones this session created (new files without flows or modules, new flows without themes, milestones without flows) before ending; report the rest to the user with counts. If a flow's description grew this session, check whether it should be split (oversized_flows).
AI should use returned watchdog reminders (if any) to address outstanding issues.
AI should generate session summary from returned data and present to user.
AI handles all FP compliance checking — helper only returns code data for AI to review.
Once complete, Inform user safe to end session.
implementation_notes: NO analysis or compliance logic — pure data gathering and process management

Step 1: Read .aimfp-project/watchdog/watchdog.pid — if PID file exists and process alive, read .aimfp-project/watchdog/reminders.json, then kill process. If PID file absent, set watchdog_stopped=null (not implemented/not running)
Step 2: Query files table — SELECT id, path, updated_at, is_reserved FROM files
Step 3: Query functions table — SELECT id, name, file_id, is_reserved FROM functions
Step 4: Query active tasks/items — SELECT from tasks, items WHERE status='in_progress'
Step 5: Query recent notes — SELECT from notes ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10
Step 6: Read project metadata — SELECT status, version from project table
Step 7: Return structured audit data object
RETURN STRUCTURE: {success: bool, watchdog: {stopped: bool|null, final_reminders: []}, project_state: {files: [], functions: [], active_tasks: [], active_items: [], recent_notes: [], metadata: {}}}
ERROR RETURN: {success: false, error: str, partial_data: {}|null}
Watchdog handling is graceful: if no watchdog is running for this project, the PID file won't exist — return watchdog.stopped=null
All operations are DB reads + one process kill — no writes except clearing reminders.json

helpers.name: clear_watchdog
helpers.purpose: Clear watchdog reminders after they have been reviewed and handled. Reminders persist in .aimfp-project/watchdog/reminders.json until this is called. Call after addressing all watchdog findings (file deletions, unregistered files, etc.).
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if project root not established
return_statements: Watchdog reminders cleared. Resume normal workflow.
The structure_gaps reminder is recomputed from project.db at the next checkpoint: clearing it does not resolve the gaps. Fix them (get_structure_health lists them all) and it disappears on its own.
